subject: Svenska
title: Correct Swedish usage
sourceSummary: De, dem and dom, incorrect word splitting, comma splices, and commas with subordinate clauses. Here you also practise distinguishing spoken language from written language in school assignments.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct word: "Vi hälsade på ___ under sommarlovet."
questions.opener: The word comes after the preposition "på" — try replacing it with "oss" or "vi".
choices: dem
de
dom
dessa de
questions.explanation: After a preposition, the object form is used: "dem". The test also works with vi/oss — "vi hälsade på oss" shows that the object form is needed, so not "de".

questions.prompt: Which sentence is correctly written for a school assignment?
questions.opener: Think about both whether the word is a subject or an object, and whether the form belongs in writing.
choices: Dom sa att dom skulle komma.
De sa att de skulle komma.
Dem sa att dem skulle komma.
De sa att dem skulle komma.
questions.explanation: In both clauses the word is a subject — it is de who say and de who will come — so "de" both times. "Dom" works in speech and in fictional dialogue, but in school assignments de/dem is expected.

questions.opener: Read the words aloud: if you hear a stress dip in the middle, it's probably a compound word.
choices: Han köpte en ny cykel hjälm.
Han köpte en ny Cykelhjälm.
Han köpte en ny cykelhjälm.
Han köpte en ny cykels hjälm.
questions.explanation: "Cykelhjälm" is a compound word and is written as one word. Writing "cykel hjälm" turns it into two separate things, roughly as if he had bought both a bike and a helmet.

questions.prompt: What is wrong with the sentence? "Jag hann inte äta frukost, bussen gick tidigare idag."
questions.opener: Look at what's on either side of the comma — could both parts stand as their own sentences?
choices: Incorrect word splitting
Incorrect use of de and dem
The sentence is missing a subject
A comma splice — two main clauses joined by only a comma
questions.explanation: Both parts are complete main clauses, so a comma alone is not enough. Fix it with a full stop, a semicolon, or a conjunction: "...frukost, för bussen gick tidigare idag." There is neither a word-splitting error nor a de/dem error in the sentence.

questions.prompt: Where should the comma go? "Om du hinner före mig ___ kan du börja utan mig."
questions.opener: The sentence opens with a subordinate clause — where does it end?
choices: After "Om"
After "mig" (the first time)
After "kan"
No comma is needed at all
questions.explanation: The subordinate clause "Om du hinner före mig" comes first and ends with a comma before the main clause begins. A comma after "Om" would cut straight through the subordinate clause, which is never correct.

questions.prompt: Which phrasing belongs in a written text?
questions.opener: Certain small words carry over from speech but count as mistakes or carelessness in writing.
choices: Hon är störst utav alla i laget.
Hon är störst utav dom alla i laget.
Hon är störst av alla i laget.
Hon är den störste utav alla i laget.
questions.explanation: It's "av", not "utav" — "utav" is colloquial and should be avoided in writing. The same goes for "dom", "ba", "typ" and "asså", which belong in speech but not in a submitted assignment.

questions.prompt: Correct the sentence and explain every change: "Dom som var sena fick inte följa med, dem andra åkte iväg direkt utav glädje på en klass resa."
questions.opener: Look for four types of errors: dom in writing, de/dem errors, comma splices and incorrect word splitting.
questions.answer: De som var sena fick inte följa med. De andra åkte iväg direkt av glädje på en klassresa.
steps: "Dom som var sena" → "De som var sena". The word is a subject, and "dom" is spoken language that doesn't belong in a school assignment.
"fick inte följa med, dem andra åkte" → put a full stop after "med". Two complete main clauses may not be joined together with just a comma (a comma splice).
"dem andra" → "De andra". It is they who go off, i.e. a subject — test with "they", not "them".
"klass resa" → "klassresa". A compound word that should be written as one.

questions.prompt: What rules and tricks do you use for de/dem, incorrect word splitting, comma splices and commas with subordinate clauses?
questions.opener: Four common traps — one memory rule for each.
questions.answer: De/dem · replace with vi/oss or they/them · if it becomes "vi"/"they" you write de, if it becomes "oss"/"them" you write dem · after a preposition (med, till, av, på, för) always dem · "dom" belongs to speech, not to the school assignment. Incorrect word splitting · if the words belong together as ONE thing they are written together (klassresa, cykelhjälm) · splitting the word changes the meaning. Comma splices · two main clauses may not be held together by just a comma · fix it with a full stop, semicolon or a conjunction (och, men, för, så). Comma with a subordinate clause · a subordinate clause before the main clause ends with a comma ("När vi kom hem, åt vi") · an inserted subordinate clause is framed by commas on both sides. Spoken language in writing · avoid utav, dom, typ, ba, asså.
